evidence.quote: | Ok(Json.Object _ as file) when Codec.text "schema" file = Ok Schema ->
| Some b -> not (b.Books.Customers.IsEmpty && b.Books.Drafts.IsEmpty && b.Books.Invoices.IsEmpty && b.Payments.IsEmpty)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule is in Tier 2. This covers the file format, the version check, the data-version check, the 'new books only' check, the GitHub refusal and the Files-pack check. They sit in Summa.Storage.Transfer and Summa.Web.Engine.Accounting. The only Tier 3 change maps three event names to messages, so it decides nothing. Tier 3 calls no Ledger function and reads no Ledger fields.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with
save { model with Manifest = Some transferred.Manifest ...

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Transfer.fs is documented as 'Pure' and uses no IO, clock or random symbol. The time comes from ctx.Now. The download is an OfferDownload effect returned as data. The import goes through the existing save, which produces a SaveBooks effect. The base64 and UTF-8 conversion is pure and not banned. No new effect appears below Tier 4.

evidence.quote: let private booksOnGitHubText = "Books on GitHub are moved with their repository, not with a transfer file."

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The schema name, version and timestamp format each have one definition, and the GitHub sentence is a single constant used by both handlers. Export and read share the version and format values. The 'holds records' predicate is written once. No duplicated fact is visible in the diff.

evidence.quote: if n = decimal Version && stated <> Some actualContents then

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The counting and the contents-mismatch refusal are in Tier 2, in Transfer. The preview is also in Tier 2, in the Engine, and it only formats the counts that Transfer.read returns. Tier 3 is untouched. The counts come from the checked books, not from the file's claim, so there is no second authority.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The preview is a pure function of the pasted text and is projected in the view. It performs no I/O and reads no clock. The export timestamp comes from the file. Transfer stays pure. Nothing new bypasses a port.

evidence.quote: | Error why -> $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"
| Error why -> { model with Error = Some $"This file cannot be imported: {why}" }, []

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Most facts have one definition. The version constants are Version and FirstVersion, the counts come from contentsOf, and export and read share that function. The refusal prefix 'This file cannot be imported: ' is now written twice, once in the new preview and once in the change set 1 import handler. Line 209 is quoted from change set 1, which this change set builds on. The two copies agree, but they could drift. One shared helper would have avoided this.
